rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's eloquence, arrangement, and complete meanings exceed reason; humans and jinn are named because they deny its divine origin and are challenged, while even angels would be unable to match it.
rows.anchor: المنعوت بما لا تدركه العقول من النعوت الجليلة الشأن من البلاغة وحسن النظم وكمال المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit wording means no speech can match the Quran's qualities; naming the likeness rather than using a pronoun avoids implying one particular counterpart.
rows.anchor: وأوثر الإظهار على إيراد الضمير الراجع إلى المثل المذكور واحتراز عن أن يتوهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say naming jinn heightens the challenge: if humans fail even with jinn helping, humans alone are still less able; al-Alusi calls this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد تعجيز الإنس وذكر الجن مبالغة في تعجيزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the jinn-as-assistants explanation as unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وليس بذاك وقيل : يجوز أن يراد من الجن ما يشمل الملائكة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take jinn to include angels, citing that usage elsewhere; al-Alusi says this conflicts with the usual sense and is not the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يراد من الجن ما يشمل الملائكة عليهم السلام وقد جاء إطلاق الجن على الملائكة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exclude angels because they mediated the Quran's delivery; al-Alusi replies that the verse denies matching it, not its delivery from God by anyone mentioned.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الملائكة عليهم السلام حيث كانوا وسائط في إتيانه لا ينبغي إدراجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb answers the oath introduced by lām and fills the conditional-result position; Basrans do not allow making it the conditional answer while that lām is present.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( لايأتون ) جواب القسم الذي ينبيء عنه اللام الموطئة وساد مسد جزاء الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr's line illustrates the disputed allowance of a raised verb after a past conditional; al-Alusi notes this conflicts with Sibawayh, the Kufans, and al-Mubarrad.
rows.anchor: كما في قول زهير : وإن أتاه خليل يوم مسغبة يقول لا غائب مالي ولا حرام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the lām in al-A'sha's line is extra, not an oath-introducing lām, avoiding the grammatical objection.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الأعشى : لئن منيت بنا عن غب معركة لأتلفنا عن دماء الخلق تنتفل فاللام ليست الموطئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge covers individuals attempting alone and humans and jinn pooling their thought to compose one text; mutual aid cannot produce a match.
rows.anchor: سواء كان التصدي للمعارضة من كل واحد منهم على الإنفراد أو من المجموع بأن يتألبوا على تلفيق كلام واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mutual-support clause is circumstantial and denies success under every possible condition, including maximum cooperation.
rows.anchor: أي معينا في تحقيق ما يتوخونه من الإتيان بمثله والجملة عطف على مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says earlier people objected that the Quran did not cohere like the Torah, then claimed they could bring a counterpart; the verse answers such a claim.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أن طائفة من الأولين قالوا أخبرنا يا محمد بهذا الحق الذي جئت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Quraysh asked for a strange sign instead of the Quran, claiming they could match it; al-Alusi suggests the demands that follow may be what they meant.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أن جماعة من قريش قالوا له صلى الله عليه وسلم : جئنا بآية غريبة غير هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Irshad says the oath ends futile hopes of replacing Quranic verses and should not be read merely as reinforcing the prior statement that they could not recover revelation.
rows.anchor: أن في هذه الآية حسم أطماعهم الفارغة في روم تبديل بعض آياته ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi agrees that this is not a reinforcement of 17:86 because the oath addresses Muhammad's opponents, not the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بل لأن الجملة القسمية ليست مسوقة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بل إلى المكابرين من قبله

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf argues inimitability proves the Quran created: if eternal, it would not be within human power and so could not be a miracle.
rows.anchor: واستدل صاحب الكشاف بإعجاز القرآن على حدوثه إذ لو كان قديما لم يكن مقدورا

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf replies that wording and arrangement are created by agreement, while the debated inner speech is not the miracle; the argument therefore proves nothing about that debate.
rows.anchor: لا نزاع في حدوث النظم وإن تحاشى أهل السنة من إطلاق المخلوق عليه للإيهام

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir gives a similar response to al-Kashshaf's inference from inimitability to createdness.
rows.anchor: وذكر نحوه ابن المنير

rows.speaker: صاحب التقريب
rows.claim: Al-Taqrib denies that ability entails createdness: possibility makes something within power, the miracle is its wording, and eternal inner speech is not the challenged expression.
rows.anchor: الجواب منع الملازمة إذ مصحح المقدورية الإمكان وهو حاصل لا الحدوث

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi selects the further reply: even if humans cannot reproduce the eternal original, one must explain why they cannot produce its like.
rows.anchor: واختار العلامة الطيبي هذا الأخير في الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly presents Quranic meanings in varied forms to establish them firmly; the meanings are beautiful, remarkable, compelling, and addressed to Meccans and others.
rows.anchor: ( ولقد صرفنا ( كررنا ورددنا على أساليب مختلفة توجب زيادة تقرير ورسوخ

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes an omitted object after ṣarrafnā, estimating al-bayān; Ibn Atiyya instead treats min as extra so kull is the object, following Kufan and al-Akhfash usage rather than most Basrans.
rows.anchor: ومفعول ( صرفنا ) على ما استظهره أبو حيان محذوف أي البيان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats min as extra in the affirmative construction, making kull the object, a view accepted by Kufans and al-Akhfash but rejected by most Basrans.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن تكون سيف خطيب فكل هو المفعول

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ṣarrafnā with a light rā; the majority reading with a doubled rā is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( صرفنا ) بتخفيف الراء وقراءة الجمهور أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Varied presentation aims to make people accept the Quran, but most refuse with denial, contradicted already by its basic inimitability.
rows.anchor: فالمراد فعلنا ذلك للناس ليذعنوا ويتلقوه بالقبول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation includes the polytheists and People of the Book in Muhammad's era; al-Bahr more strongly identifies the people as Meccans because later pronouns refer to them.
rows.anchor: قيل : من كان في عهده صلى الله عليه وسلم من المشركين وأهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufūran is the accusative object of abā and the exception is free; abā approaches negation, allowing the sense that they accepted nothing but disbelief.
rows.anchor: ونصب ( كفورا ) على أنه مفعول أبى والاستثناء مفرغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception intensifies refusal: they accepted no stance such as belief or suspension except disbelief; alternatively, they refused everything proposed except disbelief.
rows.anchor: وفيه من المبالغة ما ليس في أبوا الإيمان لأن فيه زيادة على أنهم لم يرضوا بخصلة سوى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After defeat by Quranic inimitability and other miracles, the opponents offered demands that wisdom did not require, some rationally impossible.
rows.anchor: عند ظهور عجزهم ووضوح مغلوبيتهم بالإعجاز التنزيلي وغيره من المعجزات الباهرة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans read tafjura without doubling, from a transitive form meaning to open; the other seven readers double it for intensity, not transitivity.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف من باب نصر المتعدي وبذلك قرأ الكوفيون أي تفتح

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash and Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Yasar read tafjira in a quadriliteral form, a dialectal variant of fajjara.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وعبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار ( تفجر ) من أفجر رباعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite earth means Mecca, known for scarce water; yanbūʿ is an abundant spring that does not dry up, with its yāʾ serving as intensifier.
rows.anchor: أي أرض مكة لقلة مياهها فالتعريف عهدي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi defines yanbūʿ as a river flowing from a spring, transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim; the spring explanation is attributed to Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي لأن الينبوع هو النهر الذي يجري من العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden's trees conceal the ground beneath; palms and grapes are singled out because they predominated locally and were highly valued.
rows.anchor: بستان تستر أشجارها ما تحتها من العرصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers run through the garden's middle and interior, either to water it or continuously, as the coordinating fa suggests.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرفية أي وسط تلك الجنة و أثنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kisafan is a plural of kisfa, pieces; it describes the sky falling in pieces, and the comparison modifies an omitted verbal noun for the manner of falling.
rows.anchor: جمع كسفة كقطعة وقطع لفظا ومعنى وهو حال من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They allude to the demand in 26:187; the alternative that they mean 17:68 is rejected, while another view takes it as a claim that God can act if He wills.
rows.anchor: يعنون بذلك قوله تعالى ( أو تسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء ) وزعم بعضهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads yasquṭ with a masculine singular verb and raises al-samāʾ as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( يسقط السماء ) بياء الغيبة ورفع ( السماء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on kisfan's vowel: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Yaqub generally use sukūn, while other readers vary by surah; al-Nashr reports agreement in al-Tur.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب ( كسفا ) بسكون السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūn may be a shortened form of the vowelled word, or kisfan may be an adjective meaning something cut off.
rows.anchor: وهو إما مخفف من المفتوح لأن السكون من الحركة مطلقا كسدر وسدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report from Ibn Abi Hatim, explains qabīlan as seeing God and the angels face to face, paralleling another demand to see God.
rows.anchor: كما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس عيانا وهذا كقولهم ( لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas, and one from al-Dahhak, interpret qabīlan as guarantor or witness who certifies Muhammad's claim and guarantees its consequences.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن الحبر والضحاك تفسير القبيل بالكفيل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses qabīlan as face-to-face and observation; Arabs use it like a verbal noun without changing gender or number.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبرسي عن الزجاج أنه فسر قبيلا بمقابلة ومعاينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes qabīlan to mean a company or group, as a circumstantial description of the angels; al-Kashf prefers that attachment because the angels are the nearer word.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد القبيل الجماعة كالقبيلة فيكون حالا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-A'raj reads qubulan, from muqābala, supporting the face-to-face interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج ( قبلا ) من المقابلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and others explain zukhruf as gold; it originally means adornment and came to mean gold because gold is desired as adornment.
rows.anchor: من ذهب كما روي عن ابن عباس وقتادة وغيرهما وأصله الزينة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reads min dhahab; al-Bahr treats it as a gloss rather than a reading because it conflicts with the codex text.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( من ذهب ) وجعل ذلك في البحر تفسيرا لا قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarqā fi al-samāʾ means climbing its ladders, with the word for ladders understood; samāʾ may also mean any elevated place or thing.
rows.anchor: أي تصعد في معارجها فحذف المضاف يقال رقي في السلم والدرجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem witnesses that any elevated thing can be called a sky; its poet is not named.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : وقد يسمى سماء كل مرتفع وإنما الفضل حيث الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would not believe the ascent either because of the ascent alone or because they would not credit that it occurred.
rows.anchor: أي لأجل رقيك فيها وحده أو لن نصدق رقيك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand a book from the sky in their language and idiom that confirms Muhammad's claim.
rows.anchor: حتى تنزل ( منها ( علينا كتابا نقرؤه ( بلغتنا عن أسلوب كلامنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥāna rabbī expresses amazement at their stubbornness or declares God transcendent above impossible demands, signaling their proposal's falsehood.
rows.anchor: تعجبا من شدة شكيمتهم وفرط حماقتهم ( سبحان ربي ( أو قل ذلك تنزيها لساحة الجلال

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read qāla subḥāna rabbī, making this explicitly the Prophet's reply.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر ( قال سبحان ربي ) أي قال النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a human messenger like earlier messengers; they performed only the signs God disclosed according to wisdom, without controlling Him.
rows.anchor: كسائر الرسل عليهم السلام وكانوا لا يأتون قومهم إلا بما يظهره الله تعالى على أيديهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats human as a setup for the main point, messenger: Muhammad was human like preceding messengers, refuting denial that a prophet may be human.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال الزمخشري هل كنت إلا رسولا كسائر الرسل بشرا مثلهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some make human and messenger independent predicates, respectively denying power to perform the demands personally or to control God; al-Alusi objects that this conflicts with reports and sound syntax.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض أن ذكر ( بشرا ) ليس للتوطئة فإن طلب القوم منه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji rejects two independent predicates because this implies they denied each property separately, while nobody denied Muhammad's humanity.
rows.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : إن كون الإسمين خبرين غير متوجه لأنه يقتضي استقلالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi replies that demanding acts beyond human capacity effectively treated Muhammad's humanity as incompatible with prophethood.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنهم لما طلبوا منه عليه الصلاة والسلام مما لا يتأتى من البشر كالرقي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A grammarian makes بشر an advanced circumstantial of an indefinite noun, but al-Alusi calls this awkward because it implies another state besides humanity.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون بشرا حالا من النكرة وسوغ ذلك تقدمه عليها وهو ركيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same group likely made all the demands, though individuals may have proposed different ones; all are included because each accepted the others' demands.
rows.anchor: والظاهر اتحاد القائل لجميع ما تقدم ويحتمل عدم الاتحاد بأن يكون بعض اقترح شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Mansur and others transmit from Ibn Jubayr that the demands passage was revealed about Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, apparently its speaker; collective pronouns still fit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جبير أن قوله تعالى : ( وقالوا لن نؤمن لك ) الخ نزل في عبد الله بن أبي أمية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports named Quraysh leaders met Muhammad after sunset, accused him of dividing the community, and offered wealth, leadership, kingship, or healing if he sought worldly gain or suffered delusion.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن إسحق وجماعة عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن عتبة وشيبة ابني ربيعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Muhammad says God sent him with a book as bearer and warner; Quraysh then demand mountains removed, land widened, rivers, and ancestors raised to test him.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما بي ما تقولون ما جئتكم بما جئتكم به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The group next asks for an angel to validate Muhammad and for gardens, treasure, or gold palaces; he refuses, saying these are not his mission and he awaits God's judgment.
rows.anchor: فخذ لنفسك فاسأل ربك أن يبعث ملكا يصدقك بما تقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They demand the sky fall, God and angels appear, or a ladder to heaven with a written book and angel witnesses; Muhammad leaves grieving after Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya says he will not believe otherwise.
rows.anchor: قالوا : فتسقط السماء كما زعمت إن ربك إن شاء فعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report says Quraysh expected a response from a man called al-Rahman in Yamama and vowed never to believe in him; these demands are followed by the revelation of 13:30–31.
rows.anchor: فقد بلغنا أنه إنما يعلمك هذا رجل باليمامة يقال له الرحمن وإنا والله لا نؤمن بالرحمن أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yuʾminū is the object of manaʿa; idh may mark the time of the hindrance or belief, when revelation and its confirming miracles arrived.
rows.anchor: أن يؤمنوا ( مفعول منع وقوله تعالى : ﴿ إذ جاءهم الهدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shared belief that a human cannot be a messenger—not one person's remark preventing others—was the obstacle; calling it speech exposes unsupported words without substance.
rows.anchor: بل المانع هو الإعتقاد الشامل للكل المستتبع لهذا القول منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names the main obstacle because it was their objection after hearing that Muhammad was a human messenger; reversing the answer shows their defiance.
rows.anchor: وحصر المانع فيما ذكر مع أن لهم موانع شتى لما أنه معظمها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say they did not reject other prophets or that the words were a rebuke spoken by Muhammad; al-Alusi finds the second view unacceptable and the first contrary to the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وصرح بعضهم بأنهم لم ينكروا إرسال غيره صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests Muhammad said this as reproach and lament; al-Alusi rejects that attribution.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من كلام ابن عطية أن هذا الكلام منه عليه الصلاة والسلام قاله على معنى التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is first told to explain God's wisdom: imagine angels living settled on earth and walking as humans rather than flying to heaven.
rows.anchor: ( قل ( لهم أولا من قبلنا تبيينا للحكمة وتحقيقا للحق المزيح للريب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i reads settled as secure in worldly pleasures, without fear or religious duties; al-Alusi prefers the plain sense of residing on earth.
rows.anchor: وقال الجبائي أي مطمئنين إلى الدنيا ولذاتها غير خائفين ولا متعبدين بشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the first reading, settled residence, over al-Jubba'i's account of worldly ease.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأول أولى وإن زعم خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would send an angel to teach what angels cannot know independently; corresponding nature makes reception easy, so only specially prepared humans receive from angels and convey to others.
rows.anchor: يعلمهم مالا تستقل قدرهم بعلمه ليسهل عليه الإستماع به والتلقي منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making everyone capable of angelic reception would defeat wisdom; angels can appear as humans, as Gabriel appeared as Dihya.
rows.anchor: وجعل كل البشر كذلك مخل بالحكمة وأنزال الملك عليهم على وجه يسهل التلقي منه

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that an unknown traveler asked the Prophet about Islam, faith, and excellence; the Prophet later identified him as Gabriel teaching the Companions their religion.
rows.anchor: وقد صح أن أعرابيا جاء وعليه أثر السفر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسأله عن الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appearance of an angel as a man would not resolve the opponents' demand, as 6:9 says God would make an angel human and confuse them as they confuse themselves.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى جده ( ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون )

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi cites a view that Arabs complained Muhammad disturbed their peaceful lives; God answers that settled angels would still receive messengers, so settlement cannot block the mission.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبرسي عن بعضهم أنه قال في الآية : إن العرب قالوا كنا ساكنين مطمئنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the peaceful-life interpretation is remote from context and unsupported by transmitted evidence.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن هذا بمراحل عن السياق ولا يصح فيه أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malakan may be a delayed circumstantial description of rasūlan, or the object of sending with rasūlan adjectival; exegetes prefer the first because it explicitly states the intended contrast.
rows.anchor: ونصب ( ملكا ) يحتمل أن يكون على الحالية من رسولا الواقع مفعولا لنزلنا

rows.speaker: القطب
rows.claim: Al-Qutb and al-Taqrib explain the word order as stressing the objection to a human messenger and the answer that the messenger to angels would be an angel.
rows.anchor: ووجه ذلك القطب وصاحب التقريب بأنه على الحالية يفيد المقصود بمنطوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that the verse restricts messengers to matching species would conflict with Muhammad's established mission to jinn; al-Alusi says it only answers opponents who insisted humans require an angel.
rows.anchor: واستشكل بعضهم هذه الآية بأنها ظاهرة في أنه إنما يرسل إلى كل قبيل لا يناسبه ويجانسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correspondence makes reception easy but is not an absolute limit: Muhammad could meet jinn after they assumed forms, and his capacities suit conveying to them.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي بعثته صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الجن لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام متى صح فيه المناسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Subki, al-Barizi, al-Mahalli, Ibn Taymiyya, Ibn Muflih, and Abd al-Haqq hold that Muhammad was also sent to angels, given his capacity to receive from and convey to them.
rows.anchor: وإلى كونه عليه الصلاة والسلام مرسلا إليهم ذهب من الشافعية تقى الدين السبكي والبارزي

rows.speaker: ابن تيمية
rows.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says scholars do not dispute that jinn are subject to commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال كابن التيمية : لا نزاع بين العلماء في جنس تكليفهم بالأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم اللقاني
rows.claim: Al-Laqqani affirms practical duties for jinn but treats faith as self-evident and therefore not an object of obligation.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم اللقاني لا شك في ثبوت أصل التكليف بالطاعات العملية في حقهم

rows.speaker: السبكي
rows.claim: Al-Subki says jinn receive the full law because Muhammad's mission is universal; prayer, qualifying zakat, pilgrimage, fasting, and prohibitions apply when their conditions exist.
rows.anchor: وقال السبكي في فتاويه : الجن مكلفون بكل شيء من هذه الشريعة

rows.speaker: السبكي
rows.claim: Al-Subki distinguishes angels: universal mission does not establish every human duty for them, though a particular mission remains possible.
rows.anchor: بخلاف الملائكة فإنا لانلتزم أن هذه التكاليف كلها ثابتة في حقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn might receive law through angels, though not every revelation came through an angel; some duties could have been conveyed directly.
rows.anchor: ولا مانع من أن يكلفهم كلهم بما جاءه من ربه جل جلاله بواسطة بعضه

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Kirmani deny Muhammad was sent to jinn; some later authorities report consensus for this position.
rows.anchor: وبعدم الإرسال إليهم جزم الحليمي والبيهقي من الشافعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal warning in 25:1 and a Muslim report that Muhammad was sent to all creation support his mission to jinn and, for some scholars, angels.
rows.anchor: وصريح آية ( ليكون للعالمين نذيرا ) إذ العالم ما سوى الله تعالى وصفاته وخبر مسلم

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some argue that the verse assigns an angel to angels and excludes a human messenger; al-Alusi replies it only requires an angel in the stated hypothetical.
rows.anchor: وقد ادعى بعض الناس أن الآية تؤيد مذهبهم لأنه تعالى خص فيها الملك بالإرسال إلى الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending a human among angels in the hypothetical would be impractical unless he ceased to be human; an angel better enables continued contact and reception.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه إذا كان أهل الأرض ملائكة وأرسل إليهم بشر له قوة الإلقاء إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi closes by urging reflection and hoping God grants a sound resolution to the preceding dispute.
rows.anchor: وتأمل في جميع ما تقدم فلعلك توفق بعون الله تعالى إلى الجرح والتعديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a second response from the Prophet after the opponents ignored the first explanation; God alone witnesses that he fulfilled his duty by presenting a confirming miracle.
rows.anchor: ( قل ( لهم ثانيا من جهتك بعد ما قلت لهم من قبلنا ما قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the witness-to-delivery reading because it fits between me and you and God's knowledge of His servants; it may still warn and console.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأول بأنه أوفق بقوله تعالى : ( ﴿ بيني وبينكم ﴾

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji prefers the alternative that God witnesses their inner motives, warning those who raise objections from envy and status-seeking; al-Alusi says this does not displace the first reading.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخفاجي أن الثاني أوفق بالسياق منه إذ يكون الكلام عليه كالسابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says between me and you rather than between us to mark separation; shahīdan is parsed as circumstantial or specification.
rows.anchor: هذا وإنما لم يقل سبحانه بيننا تحقيقا للمعارقة وإبانة للمبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins outside the command say and explains recompense: those guided reach truth and its reward or any goal; most readers omit the yāʾ in al-muhtadī.
rows.anchor: ( ومن يهد الله ( كلام مبتدأ غير داخل في حيز ( قل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance is created in people whose bad choice and disposition merit it; no protector besides God can guide them to truth, worldly aims, salvation, or escape from punishment.
rows.anchor: ( ومن يضلل ( يخلق فيه الضلال لسوء إختياره قبح استعداده

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the plural protectors intensifies the meaning: if several cannot help, one surely cannot; the singular/plural also contrasts one true path and few followers with many paths of error.
rows.anchor: وقيل قال سبحانه : ( أولياء ) مبالغة لأن الأولياء إذا لم تنفعهم فكيف الولي الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pronouns are singular when agreeing with man as a word and plural when agreeing with its meaning; the choice hints at the unity of truth and multitude of error.
rows.anchor: وضمير ( لهم ) عائد على من باعتبار معناه كما أن ( هو ) عائد عليه باعتبار لفظه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls semantic agreement before literal agreement rare; al-Khafaji objects that an understood singular object pronoun in yudlil already supplies literal agreement.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو حيان وتبعه بعضهم أن الجملة الثانية من المواضع التي جاء فيها الحمل على المعنى

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says the omitted object of yudlil is a singular pronoun referring to the literal form man, so literal agreement already occurred.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك الخفاجي بأنه لا وجه له فإنه حمل فيها الضمير على اللفظ أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan instead makes man the object of both guidance verbs, leaving no omitted singular pronoun; both clauses may also fall under the command say.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن وجهه جعل أبي حيان من مفعول ( يضلل ) كما نص عليه في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We gather them best fits the first analysis as God's statement; alternatively it reports what the Prophet says on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( ونحشرهم ( أوفق بالأول وفيه التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that when asked how people are gathered on their faces, the Prophet answered that the One who made them walk can make them walk on their faces; this applies to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه الشيخان وغيرهما عن أنس قال قيل يا رسول الله كيف يحشر الناس على وجوههم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports three groups: walking, riding, and crawling on faces; the Prophet says the One who made them walk can make them do so on faces, avoiding every rise and thorn. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج أبو داود والترمذي وحسنه وابن جرير وغيرهم عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : يحشر الناس

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports riders who are fed and clothed, people walking and running, and people dragged on faces by angels; al-Hakim grades the report sound.
rows.anchor: ويشهد له ما أخرجه أحمد والنسائي والحاكم وصححه عن أبي ذر

rows.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة
rows.claim: Muawiya ibn Hayda reports people gathered walking, riding, and dragged on their faces; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والنسائي والترمذي وحسنه عن معاوية بن حيدة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says to reconcile the reports if possible and otherwise rely on the Bukhari-Muslim report; 54:48 concerns after entry into Hell, not the prior gathering.
rows.anchor: وليطلب وجه الجمع فإن لم يوجد فالمعول عليه ما شهد له حديث الشيخين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read gathering on faces figuratively as departing frustrated and humiliated; al-Alusi rejects this against Prophetic reports and says Ibn Abbas's interpretation may have prompted it.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الكلام على المجاز وذلك كما يقال للمنصرف عن أمر خائبا مهموما

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers literal blindness, muteness, and deafness at first; God restores their faculties later so they see Hell, hear it, and speak as other verses describe.
rows.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان كون المراد مما ذكر حقيقته ويكون ذلك في مبدأ الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: The sensory conditions may be circumstantial from the pronoun or an apposition; al-Alusi calls the apposition strained.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء كون ذلك بدلا من تلك الحال وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mouths may be sealed intermittently; figuratively, they gain no benefit from seeing, hearing, or speaking truth. Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan are cited for treating these faculties as useless, with different verses reflecting different times.
rows.anchor: نعم قد يختم على أفواههم في البين وقيل هو على المجاز على معنى أنهم لفرط الحيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan are cited for the figurative view: what the condemned say, hear, or see counts as nothing because it gives no benefit.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ذلك ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس وروي أيضا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says they are blind to the gifts of God's friends, mute about God's praised attributes, and deaf to them; some say this happens after the command to remain silent in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل عميا عن النظر إلى ما جعل الله تعالى لأوليائه بكما عن الكلام معه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their abode is Hell; every time its blaze subsides, God increases the fire, either as an independent sentence or a circumstantial clause, with the independent parsing simplest.
rows.anchor: ( مأواهم ( أي مستقرهم ( جهنم ( على تقدير جعله حالا ويحتمل أن يكون استئنافا

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi parses the last clause as a circumstantial description of Hell because Hell is presented as flaming; another attachment to the earlier clause is strained.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبرسي : هو حال منها لأنها توضع متلظ ومتسعر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan distinguishes khabat, when flame subsides, from khamadat, when embers go out, and hamadat, when the fire is extinguished.
rows.anchor: قال في البحر : يقال خبت النار تخبو إذا سكن لهبها وخمدت إذا سكن جمرها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says khabat is a subsiding flame, as though ash formed a covering; lexicons differ about whether the word means extinguished.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : خبت النار سكن لهبها وصار عليها خباء من رماد

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reports Abu Salih glossing khabat as heated, an unusual meaning against the common explanation.
rows.anchor: والغريب ما أخرجه ابن الأنباري عن أبي صالح من تفسير ( خبت ) في الآية بحميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When fire consumes skin and flesh, its flame subsides for lack of fuel; God restores them to a new form and reignites it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى كلما سكن لهبها بأن أكلت جلودهم ولحومهم ولم يبق ما تتعلق به النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says disbelievers fuel Hell; after their burning they become glowing embers, then when recreated they return to the fire's blaze.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وغيرهما عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في الآية

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Some explain recurring fire as punishment for denying resurrection: they suffer it repeatedly in visible form because they rejected proof.
rows.anchor: على ما قاله بعض الأجلة عقوبة لهم على إنكارهم الإعادة بعد الأفناء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some object that 4:56 speaks of replacing skin at maturity, not total consumption; one answer says skin is burned and annihilated before replacement.
rows.anchor: بأن قوله تعالى ( كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناها جلودا غيرها ) يدل على أن النار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another answer interprets maturity as the point when sensation would cease; al-Khafaji allows burning and annihilation at different times or in different people, or a broad figurative meaning.
rows.anchor: بأن المراد كلما نضجت جلودهم كمال النضج بأن يبلغ شيها إلى حد لو بقيت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tension with 2:162 disappears because flame subsiding need not reduce punishment; other pains may replace it. Al-Razi says the later state is greater, but fear or severe pain masks variation.
rows.anchor: وربما يتوهم أن بين هذه الآية وقوله تعالى ( لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ) تعارضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may describe increased fire rather than increased suffering; it means they are remade after each burning, expressed emphatically by increasing them with blaze rather than increasing the fire.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال : ليس في الآية أكثر من ازدياد توقده ولعله لا يستلزم ازدياد عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That punishment means either the blaze just described or all their gathering and sensory states; they deserve it for rejecting Quranic and cosmic signs of resurrection or the Prophet's message generally.
rows.anchor: ذلك ( أي العذاب المفهوم من قوله سبحانه كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا أو إلى جميع ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax allows that as subject and their recompense as predicate, the reverse, or recompense as an explanatory substitute; an omitted-subject parse is rejected.
rows.anchor: و ( ذلك ) مبتدأ أو جزاؤهم خبره والظرف متعلق به وجوز أن يكون ( جزاؤهم ) مبتدأ ثانيا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines rufāt as broken, scattered fragments, like crushed straw; here it means dispersed remains.
rows.anchor: هو في الأصل كما قال الراغب كالفتات ما تكسر وتفرق من التبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalqan jadīdan is either an emphatic cognate accusative or a circumstantial phrase meaning newly created.
rows.anchor: إما مصدر مؤكد من غير لفظه أي لمبعوثون بعثا جديدا وإما حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator of the immense heavens and earth can recreate humans, a lesser act; here the wording means restoring these same people.
rows.anchor: أي ألم يتفكروا ولم يعلموا أن الله تعالى الذي قدر على خلق هذه الأجرام

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some take mithlahum as in the idiom mithluka lā yabkhal, meaning God can create them again; al-Alusi says this is somewhat remote.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : مثل هنا مثلها في مثلك لا يبخل أي قادر على أن يخلقهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says God can create other servants who worship Him and acknowledge His power; al-Alusi says this does not fit context.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المراد قادر على أن يخلق عبيدا آخرين يوحدونه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers denied reassembling scattered body parts and bones and restoring life; the proof supports bodily resurrection by recombining the original particles.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية أن الكفرة أنكروا إعادتهم إلى يوم القيامة على معنى جمع أجزائهم المتفرقة

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A minority view says resurrection reassembles original particles, preserved from becoming part of another body; al-Amidi reports it tentatively, while al-Razi prefers it.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا تكون الآية أحد أدلة من يقول : إن الحشر بإعادة أجزاء الأبدان التي تتفرق

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Sunni judge and Abu al-Hudhayl take annihilation without a contrary or condition: God commands the substance to perish, as He commands be and it is.
rows.anchor: فذهب إلى الأخير القاضي من أهل السنة وأبو الهذيل من المعتزلة قالا : إن الله يعدم ما يريد

rows.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة
rows.claim: Most Mu'tazilites instead explain annihilation through a contrary called nonexistence, which brings the substance to an end.
rows.anchor: وذهب جمهور المعتزلة إلى الأول فقالوا : إن فناء الجوهر بحدوث ضد له وهو الفناء

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Most theologians hold God annihilates bodies utterly and recreates them; al-Razi, al-Zarkashi, and al-Laqqani call this sound or orthodox.
rows.anchor: والذاهبون إلى هذا هم الأقل وحكاه الآمدي بصيغة قيل لكن رجحه الفخر الرازي

rows.speaker: ابن شبيب
rows.claim: Ibn Shabib says God creates a distinct annihilation in each individual substance, which ceases in the next moment.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن شبيب : إنه تعالى يحدث في كل جوهر بعينه فناء يقتضي عدم الجوهر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali posits one unlocated annihilation destroying all substances; Abu Hashim instead posits a separate unlocated annihilation for each substance.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو علي وأتباعه : إن الله سبحانه يخلق فناء واحدا لا في محل

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Imam al-Haramayn, most Sunnis, Bishr al-Muraysi, and al-Ka'bi say annihilation results when a persistence condition is not renewed; they differ on where persistence exists.
rows.anchor: وذهب إمام الحرمين وأكثر أهل السنة وبشر المريسي والكعبي من المعتزلة إلى الثاني

rows.speaker: بشر المريسي
rows.claim: Bishr says persistence is created outside a substrate; without it, the substance ceases.
rows.anchor: فقال بشر : إنه بقاء يخلقه سبحانه لا في محل فإن لم يخلقه عدم الجوهر

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi and most proponents say persistence is created in each substance moment by moment; without it, the substance disappears.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثر والكعبي : إنه بقاء قائم بالجوهر يخلقه جل وعلا فيه حالا فحالا

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Al-Haramayn says bodies must continually receive their necessary accidents; when God stops creating them, the body ceases.
rows.anchor: وقال إمام الحرمين : إنه الإعراض التي يجب اتصاف الجسم بها

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam says substances themselves are continually created alongside accidents; without renewed creation, they perish.
rows.anchor: وقال النظام : إنه خلق الله تعالى الجوهر حالا فحالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi regards most theories as false, especially independent annihilation entities and persistence existing outside a substrate.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن أكثر هذه الأقاويل من قبيل الأباطيل سيما القول بأن الفناء أمر محقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence from 28:88 and 55:26 is inconclusive: ruin can mean losing ordinary properties, and separating body parts can also be called ruin or annihilation.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا لهذا المذهب بقوله سبحانه ( كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه ) وقوله تعالى ( كل من عليها فان )

rows.speaker: أهل هذا المذهب
rows.claim: Their reply is that the disbelievers rhetorically stated the lesser impossibility: if resurrection after bones and fragments were impossible, it would be even more so after annihilation.
rows.anchor: وأجابوا عن الآية بأن الكفار اكتفوا بأقل اللازم وأرادوا المبالغة في الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The philosophers' proof that recreating an annihilated entity is impossible is rejected by Muslim arguments; annihilation in the cited verses can mean loss of ordinary qualities.
rows.anchor: ولا يرد عليهم أن إعادة المعدوم محال لما ذكر الفلاسفة من الأدلة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The two Sahih collections report that everything in a person decays except the tailbone, from which creation begins; Muslim also says earth consumes all but that bone, from which reconstruction proceeds.
rows.anchor: لحديث الصحيحين ليس من الإنسان شيء إلا يبلى إلا عظما واحدا وهو عجب الذنب

rows.speaker: المزني
rows.claim: Al-Muzani says even the tailbone perishes, but without soil; it may be recreated before reconstruction, so the hadith does not prove it persists. Ibn Qutayba agrees.
rows.anchor: وصحح المزني أنه يفنى أيضا وتأول الحديث بأن المراد منه أن كل الإنسان يبلى بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says hadith wording apparently indicates the tailbone never perishes; some scholars nevertheless suspend judgment on resurrection's mechanics.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن ظواهر الأخبار تدل على عدم فنائه مطلقا وتوقف بعض العلماء عن الجزم

rows.speaker: السعد
rows.claim: Al-Sa'd says no decisive evidence establishes annihilation and recreation or preservation and reassembly; al-Jurjani's commentary adopts this position.
rows.anchor: وقال السعد : إنه الحق وهو اختيار إمام الحرمين وفي المواقف وشرحه للسيد السند

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says both annihilation and recreation, and preservation with renewed accidents, are possible; scripture decisively chooses neither.
rows.anchor: وقال حجة الإسلام الغزالي في كتابه الاقتصاد : فإن قيل ما تقولون هل تعدم الجواهر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view combines both: recreate what was annihilated and reassemble what was scattered; al-Alusi calls this a good account.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الحق وقوع الأمرين جميعا إعادة ما انعدم بعينه وإعادة ما تفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term means resurrection and gathering or death; as death, it is generic because each person has a distinct end, and it can name life's duration or endpoint.
rows.anchor: وهو ميقات إعادتهم وحشرهم أو موتهم وهو على هذا اسم جنس لأن لكل أحد أجلا للموت يخصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No doubt means doubt is improper for the reflective or is categorically denied; the clause coordinates with the prior statement despite a grammatical objection to joining declarative and interrogative forms.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي الريب فيه والإنكار لمن تدبره أو النفي على ظاهره والجملة معطوفة على ( أو لم يروا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason establishes God's ability to restore them and God's truthful promise makes the appointed resurrection certain; if the term is death, death and recompense are inevitable, so they were not created purposelessly.
rows.anchor: قد علموا بدليل العقل أن الله تعالى قادر على إعادتهم وقد جعل أجلا لها لا ريب فيه

rows.speaker: القطب
rows.claim: Al-Qutb prefers coordinating with what follows the verbal particle because it is nearer and places the term under God's power and their knowledge; al-Alusi rejects this.
rows.anchor: وزعم القطب أن الأولى العطف على ما بعد أن المصدرية أما أولا فلأنه أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers replaces their expected pronoun to indict them for exceeding every limit; kufūran means denial.
rows.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع ضميرهم تسجيلا عليهم بالظلم وتجاوز الحد بالمرة
